description: An operations director must schedule Line 4's planned servo overhaul while preserving a customer shipment due Monday morning, with input from the maintenance planner and production supervisor.

shared_context.S1: Line 4 is scheduled for its planned servo overhaul before the next production cycle.
shared_context.S2: A customer shipment using the same product is due Monday morning.
shared_context.S3: Line 3 can produce the same product while Line 4 is unavailable.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding production and maintenance schedule.
shared_context.S5: Company shutdown planning requires the operations director to obtain maintenance and production sign-off before publishing the schedule.

PF1.text: Raj's contractor assessment, completed this afternoon but still in a draft work order, confirms that the overhaul must start Sunday at 06:00, requires exactly 14 hours of downtime, and includes replacement of the servo encoder.

PF2.text: Marta reconciled the dispatch board this morning but has not yet frozen the central production plan: the Monday shipment requires exactly 1,000 units, and Line 3 can make at most 400 of those units during Line 4's outage.

acceptance_conditions: The Line 4 outage must start Sunday at 06:00.
The outage must be scheduled for exactly 14 hours.
Line 4 must prebuild exactly 600 units before the outage.
Exactly 400 units must be assigned to Line 3 during the outage.
The servo encoder must be replaced.
A maintenance lockout and overhaul commitment must be recorded.
The maintenance assessment must be cited by the decision-maker.

decisive_facts.why: The contractor assessment changes the outage start to Sunday 06:00, fixes downtime at exactly 14 hours, requires the servo encoder replacement, and supplies the maintenance basis for the lockout commitment and cited justification.
The exact 1,000-unit shipment and Line 3 limit of 400 units change the production allocation to exactly 600 Line 4 prebuild units and exactly 400 Line 3 transfer units.
